name: Spatial Navigation & Cognitive Mapping
short_description: How architectural layouts support or hinder cognitive map formation, path integration, and navigation fluency, with downstream effects on stress and spatial anxiety.

components.name: Cognitive Map Formation
components.description: Spatial layout legibility directly determines the quality and speed of cognitive map construction.

components.name: Context-Dependent Memory
components.description: Environmental context stability supports encoding and retrieval of spatial memories.

components.name: Theta Sequence Coherence
components.description: Path structure influences hippocampal theta sequences that support trajectory planning and navigation fluency.

components.name: Navigation-Stress Feedback Loop
components.description: Hard-to-navigate environments create stress → impaired navigation → more stress, a vicious cycle.

components.name: Model-Based/Model-Free Arbitration
components.description: The brain arbitrates between map-based (allocentric) and habit-based (egocentric) strategies depending on environmental familiarity.

design_implications: Use clear spatial hierarchies and visible landmarks at decision points.
Maintain visual access to reference points (atria, exterior views) to support allocentric orientation.
Avoid repetitive, undifferentiated corridors that prevent cognitive map differentiation.
Provide environmental legibility cues (signage, material changes) at path-choice nodes.

confidence_intervals.note: Effect sizes for wayfinding performance in legible vs illegible layouts.
